title: Classical and Quantum Simulation of All-to-All Quantum Dynamics in Logarithmic Space
authors: Maximilian Lutz, Rahul Trivedi, J. Ignacio Cirac
abstract: We study both the classical and the quantum complexity of the problem of estimating disorder-averaged quench dynamics for all-to-all spin Hamiltonians such as quantum Hopfield, Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) or Dicke-type models. Disorder averaging restores permutation invariance in this setting, so states of $N$ spins can be stored in $\mathcal O(\log N)$ qubits. While logarithmic-space quantum computations are known to be simulatable classically in polynomial time or in polylogarithmic space, whether a single algorithm can achieve both is open, raising the possibility of simultaneous quantum advantage. To this end, we give a quantum algorithm for permutation-invariant $k$-local dynamics without disorder using polynomial time and $\mathcal O(\log N)$ quantum and classical space. We show that any classical algorithm matching these resources would imply $\mathsf{BQL}\subseteq \mathsf{SC}$. For short times, however, we provide such algorithms, including for SK models. For Hopfield models, we discuss how dilating the disorder to ancilla qubits reduces the problem to the disorder-free case on an enlarged system, thus extending both classical and quantum results to them. We give some evidence that their long-time dynamics are non-trivial. They thus emerge as a candidate for a simultaneous time--space advantage in quantum simulation.
summary: This paper analyzes the quantum and classical computational complexity of simulating quench dynamics in disordered spin systems like the SK model. By exploiting symmetry, the authors develop quantum algorithms requiring only logarithmic space for the disorder-free case. The research aims to identify regimes where quantum computation might achieve a simultaneous advantage in both time and space over classical methods.
main_problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of estimating disorder-averaged quench dynamics for all-to-all spin Hamiltonians.
main_result: It provides a quantum algorithm for the disorder-free case using logarithmic space, and suggests that long-time dynamics of models like Hopfield are candidates for a simultaneous time-space quantum advantage.
method: The authors analyze the problem by exploiting permutation invariance to reduce state storage to O(log N) qubits and comparing quantum simulation resources against classical simulation bounds.
model_or_system: The focus is on all-to-all spin Hamiltonians, including quantum Hopfield, Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK), and Dicke-type models, whose dynamics are studied under disorder averaging.

important_parameters: The analysis covers different regimes: non-disordered ($J=0$), fixed-rank disorder ($r=O(1)$), and the thermodynamic limit ($r 	o \infty$ for SK models).
main_assumptions: The work relies on the assumption that disorder averaging restores permutation invariance, allowing for efficient state encoding.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the text references comparisons between disorder-averaged Hopfield dynamics, SK dynamics, and the LMG model.
paper_structure: The paper is structured to first define the general problem (Problem 1) and then analyze specific cases, starting with the non-disordered ($J=0$) dynamics before addressing the full complexity of disordered models.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the simulation of complex, many-body quantum dynamics in disordered systems, which is a central theme in condensed matter theory, particularly spin glasses.
